Run starts a dream:

1. An open dream whose agent is gone (ended, or its record removed) is
   closed as abandoned, and the agents of dreams that have closed are
   cleaned up. If a dream's agent is still at work, run starts nothing.
2. It gathers (see agent dream gather). With nothing new, it records a
   quiet dream, starts no agent, and says so.
3. Otherwise it records the dream and its items, writes the digest
   (.gomuxai/dreams/<id>/digest.md: each item with its key, one line, and
   how to read it), saves each memory directory as it is (commit checks
   the dream's changes against it), and spawns a Claude agent dream-<id>
   with the dream's brief, its state key dream set to the id. The agent
   works in .gomuxai/dreams, whose workspace trust run answers. It may read
   Claude Code's projects (transcripts and memory), the repos its commits
   are in and its handoff docs, edit files only in its dream's directory,
   and run git -C <repo> log or show in those repos, without a prompt.

--dry-run says what it would do and changes nothing.

Usage:
  agent dream run [flags]

Examples:
  agent dream run --dry-run
  agent dream run

Flags:
      --dry-run   Say what it would do, and change nothing
  -h, --help      help for run

Global Flags:
      --backend string          Backend for spawn or adopt: claude, aider, agy, or shell (spawn requires it or --backend-config; adopt auto-detects)
      --backend-config string   JSON file defining a custom backend (or app settings); pass it again to status/wait/watch for agents spawned with it
  -q, --quiet                   Don't print hints (results and errors still print)
      --termd-ns string         g3d-termd namespace (default: agents; never default or wall)
